report.title: Truck driver jailed pending trial over Ceuta port hashish haul
report.summary: Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta after finding bags of hashish hidden in a false bottom of his truck. report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The hashish was hidden in a double bottom adapted at the rear of the cab and at the end of the load area, and the truck aimed to reach the boarding zone carrying nothing but the drugs. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On Sunday 15 November the driver was placed before a judge, who ordered his pre-trial detention for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments.

report.body:
Customs officers stopped a Ukrainian driver at Saint-Lary-Soulan on the evening
of Monday 28 September 2026 while he was transporting more than 32 kilograms of
cannabis herb. The customs service says its officers seized 32.8 kilograms
of cannabis herb during the control. The drugs were hidden in two metal
boxes under a non-original carpet in the car's modified floor, in 32 heat-sealed
sachets, alongside rags soaked in white spirit to mask the smell, and officers
also seized 405 euros in cash. The control took place at 22:15 on a Renault
Talisman driven by a Ukrainian living in Poland with no criminal record,
returning from Spain via the Aragnouet-Bielsa tunnel. The driver said he
had been recruited on Telegram and paid 3,000 euros to collect the drugs in
Alicante and take them to Poland.

He was tried in immediate appearance and, on 1 October 2026, the Tarbes criminal
court sentenced him to 24 months in prison and a ten-year ban from French
territory. Tarbes Infos says he was tried in immediate appearance, jailed
under a detention warrant, and fined twice over, the two fines matching the
value of the drugs and the cash found in the car. The court imposed customs
fines of 131,200 euros for transporting narcotics without a proper justifying
document and 405 euros for customs laundering, 131,605 euros in total. It
also confiscated the 32.8 kilograms of cannabis, 405 euros in banknotes, two
phones and a computer. La Dépêche du Midi gives the seized cannabis an
estimated value of 131,200 euros.

The prosecutor, who asked for two years in prison, said such cases are rarely
seen at this court and demanded an exemplary sentence. The defence argued
that the driver had been used by others and had not grasped the consequences of
his acts. At the hearing the judge told him he could be more useful to his
country on his return than by practising smuggling in France. A sentence
adjustment was nevertheless proposed to him under an expulsion
conditional-release scheme.

Saratoga County Sheriff's Office deputies seized 489 pounds (about 221.8
kilograms) of cannabis after a traffic stop on the Northway in Clifton Park.

Deputies stopped a vehicle Tuesday at 2:28 p.m. for following too closely and
insufficient tail lamps on the Northway. The investigation led to the
arrests of Kevin C. Wilbur, 46, of Brushton and Quinton L. Carle, 23, of Bombay.

Wilbur and Carle were each charged with criminal possession of cannabis in the
1st degree, and Wilbur was also cited for following too closely and having
insufficient tail lamps.

Both men were arraigned before Judge Jennifer Jeram in Clifton Park Town Court. Wilbur was remanded to the Saratoga County Jail, and Carle was released on
his own recognizance pending further proceedings in that court.
